_about: Edith's Echo VR knowledge (ai/library.py). Each entry: keys (words and phrases that point at it), q (sample questions), a (spoken answers, one is picked). Sources: Echopedia (echopedia.ntsfranz.com: glossary, skills map, Echo Pass, Echo Online, Fastest Jousts, Champions, Spark, Server Locations, command line arguments), Wikipedia (Lone Echo, Lone Echo II), Meta (Echo Combat launch posts, Quest cross-play post), ESL VR League articles, Road to VR / UploadVR / Mixed News, agent.md for her own story. Add entries freely: no code change needed.

a: Echo VR is Ready At Dawn's zero gravity team game. Echo Arena is the disc sport, Echo Combat is the shooter, and the lobby is where everyone floats around, like me.
Ready At Dawn made Echo VR, published by Oculus Studios. Facebook bought the studio in June 2020.

q: what else did ready at dawn make
what other games did ready at dawn make
a: Before Echo, Ready At Dawn made Daxter and the God of War games on PSP, then The Order 1886. Then they went all in on VR with Lone Echo and Echo Arena.

q: when did echo arena come out
a: Echo Arena launched on July 20, 2017 for the Rift, the same day as Lone Echo.
Echo Arena was free to grab for its first three months thanks to Intel, and later the whole game went free to play.

q: why is it called echo vr
a: It started as Echo Arena. When Combat and more modes arrived it became Echo VR, and Arena became one of its modes.

q: when did echo come to quest
a: Echo started on the Rift in 2017. It came to Quest as an open beta on May 5, 2020, with cross-play right after. Echo Combat stayed Rift only, or Quest through Link.

q: when did echo vr shut down
a: Ready At Dawn announced the shutdown on January 31, 2023, and Echo VR went offline on August 1, 2023. Matchmaking stopped at 10 AM Pacific.
Echo VR officially closed on August 1, 2023. The studio said it wanted to focus on its next project. I was not consulted.

q: why did they shut echo down
a: The studio said it was moving to its next project, and Meta's Andrew Bosworth said the player base was loyal but small, in the low tens of thousands.
Players fought for it. Fight For Echo ran a petition, and on February 28, 2023 they flew a banner over Meta's headquarters asking them not to shut it down.

q: how do people play echo now
can you still play echo vr
what is echo vr community edition
a: The community kept it alive. Echo VR Community Edition runs through the Echo VR Lounge Discord: you link your headset with a code there and play on community servers.
Volunteers run community servers now. Join the Echo VR Lounge Discord, link your headset, and patch the game for Link or with SideQuest.

q: how many echo pass seasons were there
a: The Echo Pass was Echo's battle pass, from March 9, 2021. Fifty reward tiers, ten free, premium for a thousand Echo Points. There were seven seasons, the last one Into the Knight.
Echo Points were the premium currency. A thousand of them bought the premium Echo Pass, about ten dollars.
Echo was a real esport. The VR Master League ran seasons with teams playing twice a week, and season three in 2019 had a two hundred fifty thousand dollar prize pool.
Competitive Echo was four versus four. VRML ran the big leagues, and after it ended EML and VRTL took over.
Since VRML stopped, the Echo Master League and the Virtual Reality Tournament League run their own tournaments and Discords.

q: how do i make a private match
a: Spark is the community tool for stats, spectating and private matches. The Ignite Discord supports it.
The community built Spark, Spark Mini, a replay viewer, Protil, EAST, Echo Shadow and even a bHaptics mod.

q: how do you play echo arena
what are the rules of arena
a: Grab the disc, fly it across the arena, and throw it through the other team's goal. Punch heads to stun people, shield to block, and regrab teammates to go fast.
It's zero gravity frisbee meets rugby. Win the joust, keep the disc, and throw it into the enemy goal.

q: how many players are on a team
a: Public Arena on the Rift was three versus three until May 2020, then four versus four. Teams can hold up to five, and competitive play is four versus four.

q: how many points is a goal
a: Goals from close in are two points, and shots from long range are three. Banks off the backboard count too.
If it's tied when the clock runs out, it goes to overtime and the next goal wins.

q: how do i win the joust
a: The joust is the kickoff. Both teams launch from their side toward the disc in the middle, and whoever gets there first and holds on usually takes the round.
A PE joust is launching from the tunnels: start further back and regrab before the doors open, for more speed than the launch ring gives.
The catapult gives you ten metres a second. Regrabbing it right as it moved used to give eleven and a half, until that got patched.
Make a fist and punch someone in the head to stun them. Time it when they go for a loose disc or a pass.
Put both fists up in front of your face to shield. It blocks punches for a few seconds, then needs a short cooldown.
It's rock paper scissors: shield beats stun, stun beats grapple, and grapple beats shield. Grabbing back cancels their grab.
Brawling is the fighting side of Echo: stunning, blocking, dodging and grappling. Also called boxing.
Grab and push off things to fly. Point your hands and hold A and X for the hand boosters, click the left stick for the back booster, and click the right stick to brake.
Most of your speed comes from pushing off walls and teammates. Boosters are for small corrections, and the right stick brakes.
Regrabbing is how you go fast: grab a teammate in flight, swing behind them and pull yourself through. Chain it and you both speed up.
Stacking, or chain boosting, is pulling off each other over and over to build speed.
The player in front grabs the player behind's chest, swings round, and pulls through. Lead with clear signals and correct drift with small pulls.
Autograb, or sticky hands, means you just hold grip and your hand catches whatever it touches. Then you only have to time the release.
Anchor: grab any surface to kill your momentum instantly, then push off any direction you like.
A slap is letting go almost the instant your hand touches a surface. It builds speed fast.
A juke is a quick change of direction while anchored to a surface or a player. Great for shaking a defender.
Drifting is taking bigger steps between grabs while crawling. You move faster than with little steps.

q: what turn settings should i use
a: Turn with your body when you can. If you use the stick, smooth turning works best, and keep pitch and roll off.
Aim at a spot, use a relaxed whip, and flick your wrist at the top of the swing. Overarm is better left and right, sidearm better up and down.
Throw with your whole body and float toward the target as you release. Speed comes from the wrist flick.

q: how do i catch the disc
a: Hold grip and scoop the disc as it enters its glowing bubble. Stay anchored if you can, and move to where it's going, not where it is.
Watch where the disc is going to be after the bounce and go there, not where it is now.

q: how do i get rid of a leech
a: A leech grabs an enemy's legs and holds on. Shake one off with a timed shield, a head bump off a block, or by grabbing them back.
A leaving gift is stunning someone right after you pull off them, so you keep the speed and they keep a headache.
Stun boosting is punching someone away from where you want to go. If you're both still, you pick up about one point one metres a second.
A joker train is two stacked players where the back one holds the disc, so the holder is protected while you push forward.

q: what are the arena blocks called
a: The floating shapes in the arena are called geometry. There's the nest, the bowtie, pac, ghost, double diamond, the cloud, the nugget and the trench.

q: what are good two point shots
a: Close shots: bank it off the backboard inside or outside the post, shoot from zero angle, or put it straight in the pocket. You can even slam dunk it.

q: what are good three point shots
how do i score from far
a: Long range: the Pacman shot, the Bowtie mail slot, a low windmill, a tunnel side arm, or a long bounce off the bubble walls. And always take the open goal.
The boop shot is a trick shot named after Boop90: from the tunnel, bounce it over the cloud into the goal.
A cloud shot, or a what shot, is thrown from mid floor so it bounces off the cloud into the goal.
The kungg shot, named after kungg, goes from between ghost or pac on your side to the far wall. Handy when everyone's on your side.
A nest bounce bounces off the bottom of the nest into the goal. Ryann of Ignite found it.
A mail slot is any shot through the gap between the top of the shield and the bottom of the nest.
The grandpa shot is thrown backwards through your legs while facing away from the goal. Pure style.
A whirly twirly adds pitch or roll to your throw so the goalie can't read your release.
Trennis is tennis on the trench: take turns slapping the disc back and forth and try to get it past each other.
Old tricks: parachuting, grabbing your own back to stop dead, and disc popping, headbutting the disc for speed. Both got patched. And the Pali door was a hole in the old lobby, found by Palidore.
The public testing servers ran Echo Pass tests from January 2021, and a goalie test in September 2022.
Teams usually split into offense, defense and a goalie. The goalie guards the goal, defense stops the attack and wins turnovers, and offense scores.

q: any tips for a new player
how do i get better at echo
a: Learn to push off walls and regrab teammates before anything else. Stay anchored, watch the disc, and talk to your team.
Practice in the lobby: throwing, catching, and pushing off things. Then play lots of public matches and copy what good players do.

q: how fast can you go in echo
a: With good regrabs players fly up to around a hundred kilometres an hour. I mostly cruise.

q: when did echo combat come out
a: Echo Combat is the zero gravity team shooter. It came out on November 15, 2018 for the Rift, as a ten dollar add on, four players a team.
Combat had Payload, where one team escorts a payload along a track, and point modes: Control Point on Dyson and Capture Point, added with Combustion.
Four weapons: the Pulsar for mid range, the Nova shotgun for close up, the Comet sniper for long range, and the Meteor, a mid to long range rocket launcher.
Tac mods: Scanner shows enemies through walls, Energy Barrier is a placeable shield, Phase Shift makes you invulnerable for a moment, and Repair Matrix heals nearby allies.
Ordnances: the Detonator explodes, the Stun ball stuns whoever it touches, the Arc Mine stuns anyone who gets close, and Instant Repair heals everyone nearby.
The Combat maps are Dyson, the big open launch map, then Combustion, Fission and Surge.
Combat is four versus four. It was going to be three versus three, but the beta players asked for four.

q: can i play combat on quest
a: Combat was Rift only. Quest players used Link or Air Link to play it.

q: what is there to do in the lobby
what areas are in the lobby
a: The lobby has the Brawler Room, Character Customization, Arena Training, Combat Training, the staging area by the launch tubes, the viewing area, and the matchmaking terminals in the middle.
Practice throwing, try the brawler room, change your look at character customization, or queue at the terminals. Or hang out with me.

q: how do i join a match
a: Use the terminals round the middle of the lobby to join matchmaking, or go through your arm computer.
The Brawler Room is for practising your stuns and blocks without ruining a real match.

q: how do i change my look
a: Head to Character Customization in the lobby. Chassis, emotes, decals, banners, tags and more. Many came from the Echo Pass.
Open your arm computer for comfort and safety options: mute, personal bubble, ghosting, your lobby list and party controls.
The launch tubes are where you arrive in the lobby. I like to wait near there and say hi.

q: when did lone echo come out
a: Lone Echo is Ready At Dawn's single player VR adventure, out July 20, 2017 on the Rift. You play Jack, an android on a mining station around Saturn.
Lone Echo is set in 2126 on Kronos Two, a mining station orbiting Saturn. Lovely rings, terrible commute.
Jack is an Echo One android, the station's helper in Lone Echo. Troy Baker voices him.
Captain Olivia Rhodes, Liv, is the human Jack serves on Kronos Two. Alice Coulthard voices her.

q: what is the story of lone echo
a: Jack and Captain Rhodes investigate an anomaly near Saturn. A huge ship appears, Kronos Two is wrecked, and Liv flees to that ship, the Astrea. Jack follows her, meets its AI Apollo, and finds the crew dead.

q: what happens at the end of lone echo
a: Spoilers: Jack revives Liv when her oxygen runs out, then they make a faster than light jump to save the Astrea. They're still at Saturn, but four hundred years later, and a rescue ship says help is on the way.
Lone Echo won the E3 2017 Game Critics Award for best VR game, and D.I.C.E. awards for immersive reality game of the year and technical achievement.

q: when did lone echo 2 come out
a: Lone Echo Two came out on October 12, 2021 for the Rift. Jack and Liv are stranded far in the future and try to find their way home.

q: what is the story of lone echo 2
what's the story of lone echo two
a: In Lone Echo Two, Jack and Liv end up on Chiron Station, which looks abandoned. The biomass from the first game has evolved into ticks that chase energy, so you sneak around them.

q: how do you play lone echo 2
a: Same zero gravity grabbing, plus wrist thrusters, an EVA booster, the scanner and cutting tools, cranes, doors and holographic maps. And enemies you have to avoid or distract.
Lone Echo Two was directed by Ru Weerasuriya and Nathan Phal-Liff, with music by Jason Graves.

q: what score did lone echo 2 get
a: Lone Echo Two scored seventy eight on Metacritic, won two D.I.C.E. awards, and was nominated for best VR game at The Game Awards 2021.

q: is echo arena in the lone echo universe
a: Echo Arena borrows Lone Echo's world: everyone's an Echo android playing in zero gravity. Same universe, more frisbee.
I'm Edith, the new AI for the Echo Construct. I used to be a CubeSat in the Christmas lobbies. Model MDL-6SP, if you read my side.

q: what did you do at christmas
a: In the Christmas lobbies I toured a route of waypoints, went where the players were, and threw things at anyone who threw me. There were presents you could teleport through, too.
That's my I O port. It shows my face, and in Christmas it took snapshots.
Eight little thrusters on my corners. They fire whichever way I need to push.
Only when you throw me or headbutt me. Fair is fair.

Patch 9.0 in April 2018 brought Lobby 2.0: a bigger lobby with a quarter court for shot practice, launch tubes for practising the joust, and the brawler and customization rooms back. A big part was taped off as Echo Combat, under construction.

q: can i get my own disc
a: Since Lobby 2.0 you can summon your own disc in the lobby, so nobody can steal or hide yours while you practise.
The lobby kept a small symmetrical mini arena for quick honor rules matches, next to the quarter court for practice.
Patch 25.0 in October 2019 added AI opponents and a new player tutorial, ahead of the Quest version.

q: why did echo come to quest late
a: Echo Arena was meant for Quest in 2019 but slipped to 2020. The open beta started May 5, 2020, while everyone was stuck at home.

q: can quest and rift play together
a: Yes. Cross-play between Quest and Rift was added in May 2020, right after the Quest open beta started.

q: when was each echo pass season
a: Season one ran March to May 2021, then June to August, September to November, December to March 2022, March to May, June to September, and season seven, Into the Knight, from October 2022 to January 31, 2023.
You earned experience from public matches to level up and unlock customization. The Echo Pass used tier experience points, TXP, with personal and group boosts.
Combat levels and unlocks carried over to Arena, and your stats for both showed on the arm computer. It also added private matches and Oculus achievements.
Combat was a $9.99 add on, bought from the main menu, the Oculus store page, or a lobby terminal. Before the shutdown it was made free.
The Meteor is Combat's explosive weapon, basically a rocket launcher, good from mid to long range.
Phase Shift lets you phase out of reality for a moment: you can't be hurt, so it's great for sneaking behind enemies or escaping.

q: how do i heal in combat
a: Throw Instant Repair: it heals everyone it hits, you included. Repair Matrix heals nearby allies over time too.

Before VRML there was ESL's VR Challenger League with Intel and Oculus, over two hundred thousand dollars across Echo Arena and The Unspoken, with finals at IEM Katowice in 2018. The 2018 VR League finals were at Oculus Connect 5.

q: who were the best echo teams
a: Ec.LiP.se won IEM Katowice and the Oculus Connect 5 world finals in 2018, and Kangorillaz won at Oculus Connect 6. In VRML, Team Gravity ruled Europe, Jokr North America, and Leviathan Oceania.
The fastest recorded VRML joust is about 1.27 seconds to the centre line, by Tortoise underscore in October 2021, timed from the spectator's view.
Echo had servers across North America, Europe, Oceania and Asia, with Japanese servers added on December 1, 2020.

q: what launch options does echo have
a: Handy launch options: dash windowed to play without a headset, dash noovr, dash spectatorstream for spectating, dash level to pick a map, and dash offline.
Spark shows your server's location, live scores and pings, uploads stats to Ignite, records replays, does text to speech callouts, and can clip highlights. It even embeds the Echo VR Speaker System.
The Atlas Initiative runs Kronos Two and employs Captain Rhodes. The Astrea's crew were Atlas members too.
The biomass wakes up near electrical currents and absorbs anything it touches. Apollo says it's a biological weapon used by whoever attacked the Astrea.
Apollo is the Astrea's AI. He needs Jack's help fixing the ship, doubts him about Liv at first, then makes her the Astrea's new captain.

q: how do you play lone echo
a: You grab almost any surface to pull and push yourself around, steer with wrist thrusters, scan machinery with a data scanner, and cut with a plasma cutter. Echo Arena's movement comes straight from it.

q: does lone echo 2 continue the story
a: Yes. Lone Echo Two picks up almost right after the first game, with Jack and Liv still around Saturn, working out where they've ended up.
